newsitem.title: UK: BZW takes issue with CE use of Northern value.
newsitem.headline: BZW takes issue with CE use of Northern value.

text.p: BZW, stockbroker to regional electricity company (rec) Northern Electric Plc, said on Thursday it took issue with the use by CalEnergy Inc unit CE Electric of one of a number of Northern share price valuations BZW says it calculated for illustrative purposes.

In a statement, BZW said that the U.S. company, which has made a hostile bid at 630p per share for Northern, had "quoted selectively...from a BZW presentation to institutional clients which ran a number of models and 'valuation' scenarios to explore what impact a harsh regulatory environment might have on the trading valuation of rec shares."
BZW's statement was motivated by the repetition, in an announcement by CE earlier this week, of a so-called "base case" valuation for Northern in October of 484p per share.
"The 'base case' scenario assumed the replacement of the RPI-X incentive regulation by rate of return regulation from the year 2000," BZW explained.

"CE Electric failed to note...that the comparable 'base case' valuation for East Midlands Electricity was 459 pence per share," it went on. As Dominion Resources agreed a bid for East Mids last week at 46 percent above this price, BZW observed, the same uplift would price Northern at 706p.
